text.p: Two more losing candidates have lodged appeals against alleged fraud in Lebanon's parliamentary elections, bringing the total to 19, Beirut newspapers said on Thursday.

Eighteen of them demand that the Constitutional Council overturn the results of individual races and declare them winners, and one has demanded cancellation of the entire election held in August and September.
Newspapers said the last two appeals included one by Education Minister Robert Ghanem against his rival Henri Shdeed, who won a seat from the eastern Bekaa Valley by a few hundred votes.
Ghanem was the only minister to lose in the elections, which newspapers and an independent monitoring group said were marred by widespread fraud.
